english.title: Sell / supply investigational medicinal product for administering to subject where label does not comply reg 46

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Medicines for Human Use Clinical Trials regulations 2004

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowing, or having reasonable cause to believe, that the labelling of an investigational medicinal product, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT..), did not comply with regulation 46 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004,

(A)_[sold]_
(B)_[supplied]_

it to **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF PERSON..) for the purposes of administering the product to a subject for the purposes of a clinical trial
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 49(7)(b) and 52 of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Regulation 51 of the of the Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004 provides that a person does not commit an offence under these Regulations if he took all reasonable precautions and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of that offence. Where evidence is adduced which is sufficient to raise an issue with respect to that defence, the court or jury shall assume that the defence is satisfied unless the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that it is not.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
